verdicts.argument: Price leg holds exactly. JNJ:10k_FY2025.md p.28 (printed p.23) shows Volume 8.4% / Price (3.1) / Currency 0.7 / Total 6.0% for 2025 and Price 0.0 for 2024. -3.1% x 2024 sales $88.8B (JNJ:10k_FY2024.md p.28) = $2.75B, about 2.9% of revenue: material. Series checked on each page: 2020 -2.3 and 2021 -0.7 (10k_FY2022 p.28), 2022 -0.8 (10k_FY2023 p.28; that file is fiscal 2022, filed 2023), 2023 +0.6 and 2024 0.0 (10k_FY2024 p.28). -3.1 is the worst of the six. Caveat: 2020-2022 tables include Consumer Health (pre-Kenvue), so the perimeter differs, but the ranking still holds. The rebate leg is overstated. Rollforward figures are verbatim (JNJ:10k_FY2025.md p.42: 2025 accruals 56,819, 2024 accruals 52,786; JNJ:10k_FY2024.md p.43: 2023 accruals 47,523). The growth math is right (+7.6%, +11.1%). But accrued rebates are mostly U.S., and the candidate compares them with worldwide IM sales, whose growth was cut by FX (2024: -1.7 pts) and the COVID vaccine decline. Against U.S. IM sales (+9.0% in 2024, JNJ:10k_FY2024.md p.29; +7.0% in 2025, JNJ:10k_FY2025.md p.29), the gap shrinks to 2.1 pts and 0.6 pts. The reader's own accrual-share math moves only 48.1% to 48.5%. The AbbVie peer is not comparable: its figure covers 'rebates and chargebacks', and it also outgrew revenue (9.8% vs 9%, ABBV:10k_FY2025.md p.49, p.37). So in 2025 the gap is about 1.6 pts vs 0.8 pts, not a contrast.
verdicts.correction: Keep the price claim: price swung from 0.0 to -3.1 pts, about $2.75B of 2025 revenue, the worst in six years of 10-K tables (perimeter differs before 2023). Drop or soften 'rebate accruals outran sales for two years'. Against U.S. IM sales the 2025 gap is 0.6 pts, accruals as a share of gross moved only 0.4 pts, and AbbVie's provisions (which include chargebacks) also outgrew revenue.

verdicts.argument: Quotes verified: JNJ:10k_FY2025.md p.10 has the one sentence ('In January 2026, the Company reached an agreement with the U.S. Administration...'), the press release p.1 footnote says 'Specific terms of the agreement remain confidential', the 2025Q4 call p.9 (Wolk) says the outlooks 'absorb ... the voluntary US government agreement', and the 2026Q3 call p.8 repeats it. The sensitivity arithmetic is right: $36.3B U.S. IM sales (p.29) x 1% x 0.825 / 2,429.4M diluted shares (p.85) = $0.12. Materiality problems: (1) The base is wrong. The disclosed terms touch Medicaid, TrumpRx cash sales and new-launch pricing, not all U.S. IM sales, so '1% of U.S. IM sales' is a unit with no anchor, and the '3% = $0.37' example has no source. (2) The cost is already inside the $11.05-$11.15 2026 guide (2026Q3 p.8), so it does not surprise the earnings path. What is new is the disclosure gap, not an EPS hit. (3) Minor: the 2026Q3 call cut the ETR to 17.0-17.5%, and the CFO said the 2026 share count is higher than 2025's 2,429.4M (2025Q4 p.9). Both changes are immaterial to $0.12. (4) 'Every quarter' rests on quotes from 2 of 4 calls (2025Q4, 2026Q3).
verdicts.correction: State it as a disclosure gap whose cost is already in guidance. Present the $0.12-per-1% figure as a scaling unit, not an estimate, and do not apply it to all U.S. IM sales without saying the disclosed terms cover Medicaid, TrumpRx and launch pricing.

verdicts.argument: The plant counts are like-for-like. Both are the same Item 2 paragraph with identical wording on JNJ:10k_FY2025.md p.23 and JNJ:10k_FY2024.md p.23 (U.S. IM 4 to 3, non-U.S. IM 14 to 16; MedTech 19 U.S. both years, 27 to 25 abroad). The totals tie to the geography table (U.S. 23 to 22, worldwide 64 to 63). 16/19 = 84% and 3/19 = 16% are correct. But a plant count is not production value. On the same page, IM square footage rose 4,696k to 5,245k and U.S. square footage rose 2,892k to 3,037k, so the footprint did not obviously shift abroad. J&J also has Puerto Rico subsidiaries, and the 10-K does not say whether they count as 'U.S.' or 'Western Hemisphere excluding U.S.', while AbbVie's list counts Barceloneta PR as U.S. (ABBV p.31). The 2029 date is weaker than stated. Proclamation clause (3)(e) gives zero 'until January 20, 2029' to MFN signers, but the same clause adds 'this zero tariff rate shall also apply per the terms of the agreements listed in Annex II'. J&J's release footnotes its tariff exemption with 'Specific terms ... remain confidential' (verified table R107: 'no end date stated in release'). So J&J's own end date is not proven to be 2029. After the zero rate lapses, clause (3)(b) companies pay 20% (100% from April 2, 2030), and only EU/Japan/Korea/Swiss-origin goods pay 15%. Applying 15% to every non-U.S. plant is an assumption, not the rule. The dollar figure is labelled an assumption everywhere it appears: impact.estimate ('a bound, not a forecast'), confidence_reason, and the summary ('rests on stated assumptions'). The headline candidate sentence carries no dollar figure. But 'bound' is the wrong word, since customs value, origin mix and rate could each push it either way. Arithmetic checked: 36.3 x 18.9%-26.2% x 84% = $5.8-8.0B; x15% = $0.86-1.20B; x0.825/2,429.4M = $0.29-0.41. The 'floor' subtracts the company-wide $1.2B COGS amortization (10-Q p.43) from IM COGS 4,296 (10-Q p.32) alone. The $650-750M restructuring (10-Q p.35/p.48) is a one-time cost spread to 2029 and does not say which sites close or where.
verdicts.correction: Narrow to: the IM plant count moved from 4 U.S./14 non-U.S. to 3/16 in one year (same Item 2 paragraph), while IM square footage grew and the location of Puerto Rico plants is undisclosed. The generic MFN zero rate ends January 20, 2029, but J&J's own agreement term is confidential. The $0.9-1.2B figure is an illustration at a 15% rate on a plant-count share, not a bound.

verdicts.argument: All balances verify (JNJ:10k_FY2025.md p.48, p.62, p.52, p.93; JNJ:10q_2026Q2.md p.6, p.7, p.8, p.13; 10q_2025Q2 p.6, p.13), and the ratios are computed correctly. The metric is wrong, though. Finished goods on J&J's own balance sheet are stock J&J has not sold, so a build there does not pull revenue forward and does not imply a later 'destock of sales'. Channel stuffing would lower J&J's finished goods. The comparison is also inflated. The June 2026 inventory growth (+12.9%) is set against single-quarter sales (+6.6%), but H1 sales grew 49,372/45,636 = +8.2% and H1 COGS grew 16,157/14,985 = +7.8% (10-Q p.8). So 'twice as fast' is about 1.6x. FY2025 balances include the April 2025 Intra-Cellular acquisition, so the organic build is the cash-flow line ($1,450M, about 11.7%), not 14%. AR normalised by mid-2026 (+6.7%), as the reader concedes. The tariff timetable (Section 232 effective July 31 / Sept 29, 2026) and launch stock both explain building inventory.
verdicts.correction: At most: J&J's finished goods were $0.9B above a sales-paced level at June 2026. That is a working-capital or write-down watch item, not a revenue risk, and it is about 1.6x H1 cost growth, not twice sales growth.

verdicts.argument: The 'Other Immunology' line is read correctly. JNJ:earnings/2026-10-13_a2026q3exhibit992.md p.11 shows OTHER IMMUNOLOGY US 126 (Q3 2026) vs 12 (Q3 2025), Intl 21 vs 0, WW 147 vs 12; these are quarterly, not YTD. JNJ:10q_2026Q2.md p.27 shows U.S. 85 vs 8 for the quarter and 123 vs 9 for six months. p.40 confirms the line holds IMAAVY and ICOTYDE. Speakers check out: 2026Q3 p.14, Divan asks and Cavanaugh declines. Cavanaugh's 'north of $90 million' is about INLEXZO, which the peer field uses correctly, but in the evidence list it sits next to the ICOTYDE quotes and could be misread. Math: 126/20,000 = $6,300 and 4 x 126 = $504M are right. Materiality limits: (1) the line is about 0.5% of quarterly sales; (2) the metric divides one quarter's revenue by the cumulative count of patients ever started, and patients rose from 11,000 (mid-July) to 20,000 (mid-October), so the average count on drug in Q3 was well below 20,000; (3) with no net price in the index, $126M cannot be called 'little'. It may be consistent with a normal launch. The ceiling is solid, but 'booking little revenue' is not shown.
verdicts.correction: Keep: ICOTYDE U.S. Q3 2026 sales are at most $126M, shared with IMAAVY, and management declined to break them out. Drop 'booking little revenue', and avoid the per-ever-started-patient ratio. Neither can be supported without a net price.

verdicts.argument: The label facts verify (tremfya p.8, skyrizi p.11/12, wezlana p.7, rinvoq p.1/5), and TREMFYA US 1,772 vs 989 (+79.1%) is on the 8-K p.11. The four Medicare price rows have no page and cannot be quoted as page evidence. They are machine-extracted CMS ASP file rows in data/moat/tables/partb_asp_quarterly.csv (lines 77, 81, 106, 110). The values are real: pricing/sample_checks.csv matches J1628 2025Q4 75.972, J1628 2026Q4 66.998 and J2327 2026Q4 14.011 against the CMS zip files. But they can only be cited as the CMS file plus line, never as a verified quote. Math: 66.998/75.972 = -11.8%, 14.011/14.941 = -6.2%, both correct. Most of TREMFYA's drop came between the 2025Q4 and 2026Q2 files (75.97 to 67.81); it has been flat since. Materiality fails. J1628 is the IV induction vial in Medicare Part B, a small slice of TREMFYA. Applying its ASP move to all U.S. TREMFYA sales is unsupported, because SC and Part D net price is not public. The sizing itself, $35M per point on $3,529M (p.89), is about 0.04% of revenue. The 'heavily rebated pharmacy benefit' shift is asserted, not shown on any page.
verdicts.correction: Keep only the label edge (the only IL-23 among the four with fully SC induction in CD and UC) and cite the CMS ASP move as table data from the CMS file, not as a quote. There is no material dollar finding here.

verdicts.argument: Everything is on the cited page. JNJ:10k_FY2025.md p.8 (printed p.3) has 'Royalty rate ranges from 12% to 20% of total DARZALEX net sales', $2.4B (2025) and $2.0B (2024), and 'The two patent families both expire in the United States in 2029'. JNJ:10k_FY2024.md p.8 has the same patent text but no royalty figure, so the figure is new. The CEO says 'US. DARZALEX royalties roll off in 2029' (2026Q1 p.11), which ties the royalty end to 2029; the contract itself is not in the index. Math: 2.4/14.351 = 16.7%; 2.0/11.670 = 17.1%; 16.7% x U.S. DARZALEX 8,266 (p.88) = $1.38B. x0.825/2,429.4M = $0.469, so $0.47 is right on the reader's assumptions. Two refinements: (1) The share count is the 2025 diluted count (p.85, labelled 'Adjusted average shares outstanding — diluted', which is the GAAP diluted figure), and the CFO said 2026 shares are higher. (2) The tax rate is the consolidated 17.5% ETR. A U.S.-deductible royalty is better taxed near 21% plus state, which gives about $0.45. Also, 2029 is a partial year (mid-year expiry), so the full run-rate benefit starts in 2030. The amount, about 5% of operating income, is clearly material. Xoma math: 1% x 5,155 = $52M and 5% x 5,155 = $258M, both correct (p.89, p.109).
verdicts.correction: About $1.4B pre-tax, $0.45-0.47 EPS at 2025 U.S. DARZALEX sales and 2025 shares, phasing in through 2029 with the full-year effect in 2030. The end date rests on the CEO's statement plus the 2029 U.S. patent expiry, not on a filed contract.

verdicts.argument: The wording change is real (10q_2025Q2 p.50 says 'Medicare Part D redesign'; 10q_2026Q2 p.40 says 'unfavorable patient mix and inventory dynamics'), but the inference fails on period logic. Part D redesign took effect January 2025, so 2026 year-over-year comparisons lap a 2025 base that already includes it. Dropping it as a growth driver in 2026 text is expected, not a relabel. The growth figure is cherry-picked: U.S. ERLEADA was +4.7% in Q2 but +10.2% for H1 (738 vs 670, 10-Q p.26), and the 2026Q3 call gives ERLEADA +9.4% (p.6). The 10-Q sentence the reader quotes also names 'inventory dynamics', which the math ignores. The 8.2-point gap sets U.S. growth against international reported growth, which includes FX. It then applies a one-quarter gap to a full-year base. The result, $119M, is about 0.13% of revenue, below any materiality threshold.

TREMFYA is 5.5% of FY2025 revenue (JNJ:10k_FY2025.md p.8; 5,155/94,193 = 5.5%), with a U.S. composition patent to 2031 (p.8). U.S. Q3 2026 sales were 1,772 vs 989 (+79.1%, 8-K p.11). That is material and growing. The label comparisons verify (tremfya p.6/p.8, skyrizi p.8/p.12). The SC induction edge is real, but no page shows a dollar figure tied to it, and the price side (c06) does not hold.
verdicts.correction: The pick holds. Present the fine-print edge as a driver of volume share only, without a net-price claim.

overall: Every page-anchored quote in the JNJ file verifies, and the strongest numbers hold: the -3.1 pt price swing (about $2.75B), the Genmab royalty ($2.4B, 12-20%, U.S. 2029, about $0.45-0.47 EPS), and the plant-count shift. Several candidates inflate impact with the wrong base or metric: rebates vs worldwide sales, own finished goods read as channel risk, a single-quarter ERLEADA gap, and an IV-vial ASP extrapolated to all TREMFYA. The c03 tariff dollar figure rests on a plant-count share and a 2029 date that J&J's confidential agreement may not follow.
